Subject: Hosted API: monthly band shift + burst pocket — proposal and OK to proceed

Hi Alicia / Orbis team —

Thanks again for the conversation last week. Per our run-through, attached is a concise proposal that adjusts your monthly commitment band and adds a managed burst pocket to cover transient spikes during product launches. High-level summary: 

- New monthly committed tokens: 4.0M -> 7.5M tokens (effective June 1 billing cycle)
- Burst reserve: 60M token pool (shared for 6 rolling days), billed at a discounted overage rate if exceeded
- Per-route soft-rate limit: baseline 100 rps, emergency burst to 450 rps (subject to autoscaling checks)
- Price: blended commit rate + capped burst unit price; 12-month term with 10% volume discount

I attached a 1-page commercial summary (Orbis_Monthly_Commit_Proposal_20290501.pdf). Key asks from our side to proceed: signed SOW or a PO confirming the band and billing cadence, and a short ops kickoff to finalize route-level rate limits and canary windows.

If that looks good, can you confirm procurement lead and preferred DocuSign contact? I’ll loop in engineering to draft the ops playbook for the first 30 days.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0172

Jordan —

Thanks for this. A few clarifying items before procurement will sign off: 
1) Can you confirm whether the 60M burst pool is per-account or per-organization (we have two sub-products under Orbis)?
2) How does the soft-rate limit interact with our frontend retries — will we get 429s or an adaptive queue?
3) We need an estimate for monthly baseline spend after the change (commit + expected burst utilization).

Procurement: our PO contact is procurement@orbisai.com (cc’d). We prefer Net-45 invoices. Also please send any standard SLA exception language if you’ll be granting a higher throughput target during our launch windows.

Best,
Alicia Turner
Head of Platform, Orbis AI

Jordan / Monica / Alicia —

Quick ops note based on the request about rate handling and burst semantics. I drafted an internal runbook (see attached) but key points here to answer Alicia’s questions: 

- Burst pool scope: account-level (shared across your sub-products) but we can carve per-product subpools in the first-week rollout if you want isolation.
- Retry behavior: we prefer to return 429s for sustained overage and route-level adaptive queuing for short spikes. We will, however, provide a short-lived 202 ACCEPTED pattern for low-latency decoupling on a per-route basis if you opt in.
- Soft-rate policy: baseline 100 rps per route will be enforced; during declared launch windows (2–6 hours) we elevate the route to 350–450 rps depending on autoscaler capacity. We keep a rolling 6-day burst accounting window against the 60M token pool; bursts only bill if the 6-day cumulative exceedance crosses threshold.
- Expected spend: assuming historical traffic profile + 35% launch uplift, blended monthly spend moves to ~$32k/mo (commit amortized) with expected burst usage adding $1.5k–$7k in peak months. Exact numbers are in the attached runbook.

Next steps I recommend: 
1) Confirm whether you want per-subproduct carve-outs or single shared pool.
2) Schedule a 45-min ops kickoff (eng + infra + product) — we’ll go through canary windows, rate maps, and rollback trigger thresholds.

Attachment: ops-runbook-hosted-burst-20290507.md (ops checklist + sample rate maps)

—
Vivek Kulkarni
Principal Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
